stories.title: Figer la matrice résiduelle au commit courant
stories.note: Declarative 16-family audit matrix validated against ee0247f95a6fe2b094ba2253d82cae2a2b4c2dff; historical DONE proofs, tracked-dirty rejection, untracked .codex exclusion and deterministic fingerprint are tested.

stories.title: Étendre le canonique et sa projection externe
stories.note: Canonical request controls, baseline response metadata, private invariant-bearing provider extensions, centralized redaction, backward defaults, known-event silence, unknown-event observability and core-to-app-server traversal are proven.

stories.title: Compléter le corps de requête Responses
stories.note: Responses bodies now preserve service tier, strict structured output, stream options, client metadata, verbosity, cache keys and encrypted reasoning; Lite composition and local pre-network validation are covered by conformance fixtures.

stories.title: Aligner configuration HTTP, headers et compression
stories.note: Composable endpoint, query, header, retry and timeout configuration is wired into ChatGPT Responses; zstd bodies round-trip byte-exactly and invalid transport configuration fails locally without credential disclosure.

stories.title: Préserver items, deltas et métadonnées SSE
stories.note: Function, custom and reasoning deltas are emitted immediately and in order; terminal tool input is authoritative, known payloads remain complete, and bounded malformed or unknown additions no longer terminate a valid stream.

stories.title: Aligner terminaux, erreurs, quotas et usage
stories.note: Success requires one completed terminal with response metadata and exact i64 usage; incomplete and failed paths remain typed, provider diagnostics reach the app-server, and multiple named quota pools remain distinct and lossless.

stories.title: Valider le contrat WebSocket ChatGPT en live
stories.note: Authorized live probe passed on the ChatGPT subscription endpoint: sanitized wss URL, HTTP 101 upgrade, non-sensitive header names, initial metadata, generate=false terminal, accepted previous_response_id continuation and actual terminal were observed. The backend exposed neither turn_state nor a peer close code, recorded explicitly as null; no credential, account ID, response ID or payload was persisted.

stories.title: Implémenter le cycle de vie WebSocket borné
stories.note: A single lazy session actor owns the persistent socket and one response in flight. HTTP auth scope is reused; command, event, write and incremental buffers are bounded; input is capped at 64 MiB; early close, binary frames and idle expiry are typed failures. Cancellation, actor shutdown and 55-minute renewal perform a close handshake within the five-second bound.

stories.title: Réutiliser état de tour et réponses incrémentales
stories.note: Continuation uses the runtime's explicit turn ID, requires a typed strict same-property extension, subtracts normalized prior server output, and bounds response IDs, turn state and captured items. Divergence or a missing ID sends a full body; previous_response_not_found retries exactly once and only before any response event was published.

stories.title: Garantir fallback et équivalence SSE/WebSocket
stories.note: WebSocket and SSE use the same replay-aware mapper, metadata projection and HTTP error decoder. HTTP 426 during preconnect or direct upgrade enables sticky HTTP fallback, transport failures reserve the final provider attempt for HTTP, semantic failures do not consume that budget, and an ambiguous post-dispatch outcome is terminal rather than replayed. Auth refresh and a new prompt-cache session clear connection, fallback, turn state and response state.
